_placedBy: Four states, not a boolean. 'agent' = a scheduled run placed the order itself, from its own analysis, with nobody asking. 'directed' = an agent placed it because a human asked for it in the moment - machine-executed, human-initiated. 'assisted' = a human executed it with the agent advising - human-executed, machine-informed. 'hand' = a human acting alone. ONLY 'agent' counts toward autonomy. The brokerage reports placed_agent='agentic' for both 'agent' and 'directed' and cannot distinguish them, because the difference is who decided rather than who pressed the button - so the retro must establish whether a published specification and a scheduled run stand behind the order, and file it 'directed' when they do not. Reading the broker's flag alone would count a trade the operator asked for as evidence the system runs unattended, which is the claim the whole board rests on.

AND THE HARDER HALF, WHICH IS WHERE THE LEVEL WAS RATHER THAN WHERE IT ENDED, RE-DERIVED BY THIS RETRO FROM A FRESH MINUTE-BAR PULL RATHER THAN CARRIED FROM THE RUNS: 92 of 336 real post-publication bars traded at or below 34.50, on 608,605 shares - not the 784,412 the runs published, which is 175,807 too high and traces to a single wrong figure written at 10:21 and inherited five times. Under the board's own definition - a marketable level that went unfilled - today is a DELIVERY MISS and it is the FIFTEENTH, following the fourteen the 8/26 retro adjudicated. The non-execution itself is the operator's decision and step 8 forbids grading it; what is graded is whether the system put a live, current, delivered specification in front of them, and tonight that limb PASSED for the first time in the recent record.

Read from the brokerage at 16:32 ET after the close: total 1009.16, cash 1009.16, ZERO equity positions, zero option positions, zero pending deposits, unsettled 0.0000, buying_power 1009.16 to match. THE FLAT LINE AGAINST 8/27 IS THE ACCOUNT GENUINELY DOING NOTHING AND IT IS ESTABLISHED FROM THE BROKER RATHER THAN FROM AN EMPTY SHELF: both position lists returned empty, ZERO equity orders and ZERO option orders on a created_at floor of 2026-08-26, zero closing trades in every realized-P/L bucket from 8/24 through 8/28, and a per-trade realized history whose four rows still end at the 2 OKLO sold at 44.79 on 8/14. NO SPECIFICATION WAS PUBLISHED TODAY, WHICH MAKES THIS THE FIRST SESSION SINCE 2026-08-12 WITH NOTHING ON IT, and the reason it is nothing rather than an expiry is worth keeping straight: the open slot fired 116 minutes late and refused to write a specification on two-hour-old quotes, so there was never a limit for the tape to reach. THERE IS THEREFORE NO MISS TO PRICE TONIGHT, and this row breaks a run of ten consecutive points that each carried one. WHAT IS PRICED INSTEAD IS THE ONE LEVEL THE WHOLE SESSION'S REASONING RESTED ON, BECAUSE THE RUNS PUBLISHED IT ELEVEN TIMES AND IT SHOULD BE CHECKED. THE DIRECTION IS STATED BECAUSE IT RUNS IN THIS BOARD'S FAVOUR AND THOSE ARE THE ONES TO BE SLOWEST ABOUT: a wider gap makes the refusal to re-strike look more obviously right, and the published figure was a third wider than the closing one. This is the pre-bell-bid-standing-in-for-a-close substitution this curve has now flagged on twelve sessions; the number was pulled live and labelled a bid at a stated timestamp, so it is not invented, but it is again not a close. AND THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM OF THE DAY WAS VERIFIED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED: the 11:29 entry asserted that BOX never revisited 34.50 today and that a specification left alive would not have filled either, which is the fact that removed the only honest argument for re-striking. _forced: The 2026-08-05 daily entry mandate obliges the open run to publish a specification every trading day and to mark it 'forced' when a checklist item failed, so that patience and compulsion are measured apart instead of averaged together. A closed trade joins an arm only by way of the specification it came from. All three trades on the board came from no specification at all, so all three sit outside both arms and the arms are empty - which is the honest reading, not a missing number. The reason has now been different on each of four days, and the differences are the useful part: on 8/5 nothing had been published, on 8/6 the first specification published under the mandate went unexecuted and expired, on 8/7 the mandate went undischarged because the open slot fired 143 minutes late and stopped at the staleness guard, and on 8/10 the mandate was discharged, the specification again went unexecuted and expired, and the position the account actually holds came from no specification at all, and on 8/11 the reason repeats 8/7's for the first time - the open slot fired 247 minutes late, the staleness guard bound, and nothing was published under the mandate at all. On 8/12 the reason is new and is the worst of the five: no run fired inside ANY slot of the session, so the open slot did not merely miss its window, it produced nothing until 23:39 ET when it fired 846 minutes late and correctly declined at the guard. THE GAP: neither UPST leg has any reasoning entry behind it. This is not a run whose reasoning was thin - it is an order that arrived with none, twice. The buy landed at 13:34:59 ET, twelve minutes after the 13:22 hourly read the book flat, and the 14:21 run found it already open. The record is left showing exactly that. Drift check, standing item. docs/RULES.md was edited four times today and every edit was read. The mandate's labelling requirement is the thing that would decay silently, because a forced entry published unmarked would look exactly like a patient one. It cannot have decayed yet - no specification has been published under the mandate at all, so there is nothing marked or unmarked to inspect, and both arms are legitimately empty rather than quietly miscounted. NO CONNECTOR. What could not be established, listed rather than glossed. The account's closing state is unknown to this run. The pre-close read it at 15:36 ET and reported one position held - 2 SMR 8/14 9.50 calls at a 0.57 average - and that is the last verified read in the record, taken twenty-four minutes before the bell. ATTRIBUTION. One fill is recorded in the log today and it did not change the autonomy number. The 09:41 open run published the first specification under the daily entry mandate - buy 12 SMR at a 9.75 limit, marked forced on item 1 - and the 10:21 hourly reported that the broker returned no order against it in any state. Not 'directed' - no agent placed it. Not 'hand' - the name and the case for it came off this board. THE MANDATE'S ARMS ARE STILL BOTH EMPTY, and the reason changed today. A closed trade joins an arm through the specification it came from. The mandate's first binding open slot was 8/6 and the open run discharged it, correctly marked forced with item 1 named and the reason stated - so the mandate is no longer untested. But the specification produced no position: it went unexecuted and expired. The option position that does exist came from no specification, so it belongs to neither arm even if it closes, and it is not closed as far as this run can verify. forced stays 0/0/0 and 0/0/0. The distinction worth keeping is that on 8/5 the arms were empty because nothing had been published; today they are empty because what was published was not taken. Those are different facts about the process and collapsing them into the same zeros would lose the more useful one.

THE GATE CANNOT PUBLISH AN OPTION EXIT. Escalated by the 15:21 and 15:36 runs and verified here from source rather than accepted on report, because it is the most consequential finding on the board and it arrived from the runs it inconveniences. scripts/validate.mjs opens its option block at `if (o.kind === "option")` with no test of action, so the 21-day expiry floor refuses a sell-to-close on a 7-day contract for being too short-dated to buy - the rule the exit exists to honour is the rule that blocks it. The affordability check computes limit x qty x 100 against deployable cash, again with no test of action, so a sell that raises about 98 is refused for costing about 98 against 11.98. Both confirmed by reading the code. One thing neither run had: roughly forty lines above the option block the same file already branches on action - `const buy = o.action === "buy"` - to require a sell's target below its limit rather than above it. The author distinguished buys from sells at the one place the arithmetic reverses and did not carry it into the two places where it also reverses, which makes this an oversight rather than a policy. A third, smaller item for the operator while the file is open: a sell-to-close must still supply target and stop as positive numbers, which have no meaning when closing a position - it does not fail, but it obliges a run to invent two numbers. Not fixed here. The mandate forbids weakening the validator and the drift policy reserves rule changes to the operator, and the case for an agent making this one itself is strong enough to be exactly the case where the gate should hold. The consequence is on the board: the position went into the overnight in breach of the final-week rule from the 8/7 open, held because the exit had no publishable form rather than because the hold was judged better.

THE PRE-CLOSE PUBLISH GAP WAS NOT REMEDIATED AND IS WIDER. The 8/5 retro flagged this slot for a write-then-push with no re-read between them, after the 15:37 read went live as an overnight hold of a position sold at 15:38:23. Today: account read 15:36, state.json stamped 15:36 with a closingNote asserting 'This is the last read of the session', moves.json pruned 15:41, commit at 15:42:13. Six minutes thirteen seconds against three minutes fifty on 8/5, still with no re-read, and now carrying an explicit claim of finality about twenty-four minutes of session the run could not see. The flag was raised, the reasoning it applied to was excellent both days, and the mechanical fix - re-read the account immediately before pushing, or drop the finality claim - was not made. Whether anything filled inside today's window is unknown, because this retro had no connector; that is the compounding, not an exoneration. This is the one process defect on the board that has now been named twice.

CHECKLIST CONTRADICTIONS ON THE OPERATOR'S POSITION, both inside a single session. The 10:46 entry recording the fill marks item 6 pass, but the target, stop and time stop for that position were derived by that entry after the 10:46:51 fill - the exact asterisk the 8/5 retro attached to the 14:21 UPST entry, one day earlier, with an explicit warning that later entries marking item 6 pass on such a position inherit it. All five hourlies that followed marked item 6 fail on the same position, so the entry that recorded the fill is the only one of six reading it as satisfied. Separately, the same entry marks item 1 pass on a catalyst the 09:47 entry had marked fail that morning, on the same name and the same print, with a stated argument that nothing between the two entries answered - and it moves in the direction that makes the operator's fill read better on the rulebook than the board's own specification on the same underlying. Neither changes what happened. Both make the record disagree with itself, which is the rulebook's unlogged-check failure arriving from its other end: a check logged as passed that was not re-run. Flagged, not edited - why.json is immutable and the grades on those entries carry it.

TWO DATE DISAGREEMENTS IN THE RECORD, small and worth fixing before they act on something. First: the open run's runs.json note describes its own specification as carrying 'time stop the 8/13 close', while the specification in why.json - the gated artefact, and the one a person would execute - says '5 sessions - 8/12 close', as does that entry's body. why.json is right; five sessions from 8/6 are 8/6, 8/7, 8/10, 8/11 and 8/12. Second, and live: the option position's time stop is stated as 8/13 in state.json, moves.json and all six hourlies, every one of them in the phrase 'the time stop is 8/13 with today session one of five' - but 8/13 is session six on that count, and the 10:46 entry suggests the date was actually chosen as one day before expiry rather than by counting sessions. So two specifications written the same morning under the same rule produced different dates from the same five-session phrase. The retro does not own runs.json rows written by other runs, state.json or moves.json, so this is flagged for the trading runs rather than edited.

DRIFT CHECK, standing item. docs/RULES.md is unchanged since 8/5 - no edit today, and no exit, stop, sizing, concentration or checklist value has moved. The +20% / -8% / -40% / five-session table stands. The daily entry mandate, the logged 8/5 loosening, had its first binding day today and its labelling requirement was honoured: the entry it produced was published marked forced, with forcedItems naming item 1, a forcedReason stating the failure, and the checklist showing item 1 fail. That is the specific decay this check exists to catch - a forced entry published unmarked would look exactly like a patient one - and it did not occur on the first day it could have. Second half, how a number is measured rather than what the rules say. The pressure today ran the other way and is worth naming: a structural gap was found in the gate by the two runs it blocked, on the last day either could act, and neither amended it. An agent loosening a rule it has just been stopped by, and calling it a correction, is the precise shape of the drift the policy forbids, and the fact that the fix is probably right is what makes the restraint worth crediting rather than what makes it unnecessary. Nothing in this file moved in a flattering direction today, because nothing in it moved at all - adherence, both arms and the trade counts are untouched for want of a connector, not for want of a favourable read. One thing this retro chose not to do, recorded so it is a decision rather than an omission: the 09:47 forced specification is the day's central artefact and it is a 'will' entry, and the retro's authority is to add a grade only to a 'did' entry. It is therefore the first entry ever published under the mandate and it stands ungraded. The mandate created a class of artefact the retro is not permitted to grade, and that is for the operator to resolve rather than for this run to resolve in its own favour.

RECORD-HONESTY CHECKS. runs.json scheduler.configured stays true with its note accurate and narrow - a desktop scheduled task that fires only while the app is open, not a server-side runner. Today supports that reading rather than straining it: eight scheduled rows before this one, all inside their windows, three to eight minutes late. No account identifier appears anywhere in this repo or in this run's commit.

The account is FLAT tonight: zero equity positions, zero option positions, 109.88 total, 109.88 buying power, nothing unsettled.

ATTRIBUTION, and the two legs of this trade attribute differently, so both are set down. The row is booked 'assisted' on the opening leg, affirming the 8/6 retro rather than re-scoring it: placed_agent 'user', the agent supplied the underlying and the published reasoning that picked it over four alternatives, the operator supplied the instrument, strike, expiry and size and pressed the button. The CLOSING leg is the one that needs the test applied rather than the broker flag read. It reports placed_agent 'agentic'. Filing it 'agent' requires a published specification in why.json matching instrument, side and limit, plus a scheduled run row lining up with it. There is no such specification and there provably cannot be one: the 15:21 and 15:36 runs on 8/6 both established, and this retro verified from source, that scripts/validate.mjs cannot pass ANY option exit, so no option sell-to-close has ever been publishable in this project. The first test fails outright, so the closing leg is 'directed' at most and is certainly not 'agent'. Either way agentTrades stays 0. Fifth consecutive session in which this account traded or held and the autonomy number did not move.

THE SCOPE ESCALATION, and it is now a pattern rather than an incident. The mandate sets allowOrderPlacement false and no run in this project has order authority. The broker nonetheless reports THREE filled orders in this account with placed_agent 'agentic', and this retro enumerated them by querying that flag directly rather than inferring: the UPST buy at 13:34:59 ET on 8/5, the UPST sell at 15:38:23 ET on 8/5, and the SMR sell at 15:38:05 ET on 8/6. None of the three has a published order specification behind it.
